findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket (including the seeded vendor roster) are not guaranteed to be encrypted with a managed KMS key at rest.

The bucket declares no ACL and no public access block or bucket policy, leaving access control to defaults; combined with no logging or versioning this bucket has no defence-in-depth against accidental public exposure or object deletion.
Unlike audit_trail-backed buckets, this bucket has no logging block, so unauthorised access to the stored vendor data would leave no audit record.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so sensitive financial export data is stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No logging block is configured for this financial data bucket, so there is no server access log trail for reads or writes of ledger exports.
Versioning is not enabled, so objects can be silently overwritten or deleted (force_destroy is also true), removing the ability to recover from tampering or ransomware-style deletion.
The model artifact bucket configures versioning and logging but no server-side encryption, so artifacts are stored unencrypted by default.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined; operational runbooks frequently contain sensitive procedural and credential-adjacent information and are stored unencrypted.
This bucket has no logging block, so access to runbook content is not recorded in the audit_trail log bucket used by other buckets in this file.

The ACL value "lcatalogopts-delivery-write" appears to be a corrupted form of "log-delivery-write". An unrecognised canned ACL on the central log-target bucket means log delivery grants may not be applied as intended, potentially breaking or misconfiguring access control on the audit log store.
force_destroy = true on the bucket that holds security audit logs allows a single terraform destroy to permanently delete all audit evidence, undermining log integrity and non-repudiation.
